cluster.headline: Himachal Pradesh sets licence fees for controlled cannabis cultivation
cluster.summary: Under a Department of Taxes and Excise notification, industrial hemp farmers in Himachal Pradesh pay ₹2,000 per bigha annually, licensed manufacturers cultivating their own crop ₹10 lakh per bigha, and independent medical or scientific cultivation licences ₹3 lakh per bigha. About two weeks ago the cultivation fee was cut to ₹1 lakh per bigha and processing unit fees from ₹2 crore to ₹1 crore; cultivators need at least three contiguous acres and Himachali agriculturist status.

story.headline: Himachal sets licence fees for controlled cannabis cultivation, intake note says
story.body:
Himachal Pradesh has fixed a schedule of licence fees for controlled cannabis cultivation through a notification of the state Department of Taxes and Excise, according to the intake note circulated to the desk. No wire copy has come in on this yet, and the details below rest entirely on that note.

As described in the intake note, industrial hemp growers would pay ₹2,000 per bigha a year. Licensed manufacturers who cultivate their own crop would pay ₹10 lakh per bigha, while standalone licences for medical or scientific cultivation are pegged at ₹3 lakh per bigha.

The note further says that roughly two weeks ago the cultivation fee was reduced to ₹1 lakh per bigha, and that fees for processing units were halved from ₹2 crore to ₹1 crore. It is not stated in the note which of the categories above that ₹1 lakh figure applies to, and the desk should not assume.

On eligibility, the intake note says applicants must hold at least three contiguous acres and must qualify as Himachali agriculturists. The note does not spell out how contiguity is to be established, who certifies agriculturist status, or whether leased land counts.

The note dates the original notification to July and describes the fee cut as about two weeks old. It is not breaking news. No official quotes, no notification number, no named officials and no figures on how many licences have been applied for or granted are contained in the material available.

Before anything runs, the desk needs to obtain and read the Department of Taxes and Excise notification itself, along with the later fee-revision order; confirm the exact fee for each licence category and which one was reduced to ₹1 lakh; establish the notification dates and numbers; verify the eligibility conditions and the definition of Himachali agriculturist status; and secure on-record comment from the department. The relationship between this fee schedule and any enabling state law or central approval is also unconfirmed.

blocks.label: Anchor script
lines: Himachal Pradesh has put a price on controlled cannabis cultivation.
A Department of Taxes and Excise notification, dated July, sets out the licence fees — according to an intake note circulated to our desk.
Industrial hemp growers would pay two thousand rupees per bigha a year. Licensed manufacturers growing their own crop, ten lakh rupees per bigha.
Standalone medical or scientific cultivation is pegged at three lakh rupees per bigha.
The note says that about two weeks ago a cultivation fee was cut to one lakh rupees per bigha, and processing unit fees were halved, from two crore to one crore.
To apply, you need at least three contiguous acres, and you must qualify as a Himachali agriculturist.
We are still seeking the notification itself and comment from the department.

blocks.label: Headline
lines: नियंत्रित भांग खेती के लिए हिमाचल ने तय किया लाइसेंस शुल्क, इनटेक नोट में दावा

blocks.label: Body
lines: डेस्क पर परिचालित इनटेक नोट के अनुसार, हिमाचल प्रदेश ने राज्य के आबकारी एवं कराधान विभाग (Department of Taxes and Excise) की एक अधिसूचना के जरिये नियंत्रित भांग की खेती के लिए लाइसेंस शुल्क की एक सूची तय कर दी है। इस बारे में अब तक कोई एजेंसी कॉपी नहीं आई है, और नीचे दिए गए ब्योरे पूरी तरह उसी नोट पर आधारित हैं।

इनटेक नोट में बताया गया है कि औद्योगिक हेम्प (भांग) उगाने वालों को प्रति बीघा सालाना ₹2,000 देने होंगे। अपनी फसल स्वयं उगाने वाले लाइसेंसशुदा विनिर्माताओं को प्रति बीघा ₹10 लाख चुकाने होंगे, जबकि चिकित्सा या वैज्ञानिक उद्देश्य से खेती के लिए अलग से दिए जाने वाले लाइसेंस का शुल्क प्रति बीघा ₹3 लाख रखा गया है।

नोट में आगे कहा गया है कि करीब दो सप्ताह पहले खेती का शुल्क घटाकर प्रति बीघा ₹1 लाख कर दिया गया, और प्रसंस्करण इकाइयों का शुल्क ₹2 करोड़ से आधा कर ₹1 करोड़ कर दिया गया। नोट में यह स्पष्ट नहीं है कि ₹1 लाख का यह आंकड़ा ऊपर बताई गई किस श्रेणी पर लागू होता है, और डेस्क को इस बारे में कोई अनुमान नहीं लगाना चाहिए।

पात्रता के संबंध में इनटेक नोट कहता है कि आवेदकों के पास कम से कम तीन एकड़ सटी हुई (कंटीग्यूअस) भूमि होनी चाहिए और उन्हें हिमाचली कृषक की श्रेणी में आना चाहिए। नोट में यह नहीं बताया गया कि भूमि के लगातार होने की पुष्टि कैसे होगी, कृषक का दर्जा कौन प्रमाणित करेगा, या पट्टे पर ली गई जमीन गिनी जाएगी या नहीं।

नोट में मूल अधिसूचना की तिथि जुलाई बताई गई है और शुल्क में कटौती को करीब दो सप्ताह पुराना बताया गया है। यह ब्रेकिंग न्यूज़ नहीं है। उपलब्ध सामग्री में न कोई आधिकारिक बयान है, न अधिसूचना संख्या, न किसी अधिकारी का नाम, और न ही यह आंकड़ा कि कितने लाइसेंसों के लिए आवेदन आए या कितने दिए गए।

कुछ भी प्रकाशित करने से पहले डेस्क को आबकारी एवं कराधान विभाग की मूल अधिसूचना तथा बाद में जारी शुल्क-संशोधन आदेश हासिल कर पढ़ना होगा; हर लाइसेंस श्रेणी का सटीक शुल्क और यह पुष्टि करनी होगी कि किसे घटाकर ₹1 लाख किया गया; अधिसूचना की तिथियां और संख्याएं स्थापित करनी होंगी; पात्रता शर्तों तथा हिमाचली कृषक दर्जे की परिभाषा की पुष्टि करनी होगी; और विभाग से ऑन-रिकॉर्ड टिप्पणी लेनी होगी। इस शुल्क सूची का किसी सक्षम राज्य कानून या केंद्रीय मंजूरी से क्या संबंध है, यह भी अपुष्ट है।

blocks.label: Frame 1
lines: [Wide: terraced farmland in Himachal Pradesh under morning light]
Himachal Pradesh has fixed a schedule of licence fees for controlled cannabis cultivation, according to the intake note circulated to the desk.

blocks.label: Frame 2
lines: [Mid: the exterior of a state government office building]
The fees were set through a notification of the state Department of Taxes and Excise, the intake note says. The notification itself has not been read by the desk.

blocks.label: Frame 3
lines: [Close: hemp stalks standing in a cultivated plot]
Industrial hemp growers would pay ₹2,000 per bigha a year under the schedule described in the note, the lowest of the listed rates.

blocks.label: Frame 4
lines: [Mid: a processing shed on agricultural land, doors open]
Licensed manufacturers cultivating their own crop would pay ₹10 lakh per bigha. Standalone medical or scientific cultivation licences are pegged at ₹3 lakh per bigha.

blocks.label: Frame 5
lines: [Close: a printed fee table on a desk, figures partly visible]
Roughly two weeks ago the cultivation fee was cut to ₹1 lakh per bigha, the note says. It does not state which category that figure applies to.

blocks.label: Frame 6
lines: [Wide: machinery inside an agricultural processing unit]
Fees for processing units were halved from ₹2 crore to ₹1 crore, according to the same note. No official has commented on record.

blocks.label: Frame 7
lines: [Aerial: adjoining fields separated by low stone boundaries]
Applicants must hold at least three contiguous acres and qualify as Himachali agriculturists. The note does not explain how contiguity is established.

blocks.label: Frame 8
lines: [Wide: empty hillside fields at dusk, no activity visible]
The original notification is dated to July. Figures on licences applied for or granted are absent from the material available to the desk.

brief.headline: Himachal sets licence fees for controlled cannabis cultivation, intake note says
brief.body:
Himachal Pradesh has fixed a schedule of licence fees for controlled cannabis cultivation through a notification of the state Department of Taxes and Excise, according to the intake note circulated to the desk. No wire copy has come in on this yet, and the details below rest entirely on that note.

As described in the intake note, industrial hemp growers would pay ₹2,000 per bigha a year. Licensed manufacturers who cultivate their own crop would pay ₹10 lakh per bigha, while standalone licences for medical or scientific cultivation are pegged at ₹3 lakh per bigha.

The note further says that roughly two weeks ago the cultivation fee was reduced to ₹1 lakh per bigha, and that fees for processing units were halved from ₹2 crore to ₹1 crore. It is not stated in the note which of the categories above that ₹1 lakh figure applies to, and the desk should not assume.

On eligibility, the intake note says applicants must hold at least three contiguous acres and must qualify as Himachali agriculturists. The note does not spell out how contiguity is to be established, who certifies agriculturist status, or whether leased land counts.

The note dates the original notification to July and describes the fee cut as about two weeks old. It is not breaking news. No official quotes, no notification number, no named officials and no figures on how many licences have been applied for or granted are contained in the material available.

Before anything runs, the desk needs to obtain and read the Department of Taxes and Excise notification itself, along with the later fee-revision order; confirm the exact fee for each licence category and which one was reduced to ₹1 lakh; establish the notification dates and numbers; verify the eligibility conditions and the definition of Himachali agriculturist status; and secure on-record comment from the department. The relationship between this fee schedule and any enabling state law or central approval is also unconfirmed.
